entries.mechanism: Married couple, $240,528 wages, $11,273 short-term capital gain (taxed at ordinary rates), and $46,851 of pension income. After the tax-before-credits mapping was corrected to compare Tax-Calculator's `taxbc` against PolicyEngine's [income_tax_main_rates, capital_gains_tax] sum, the residual is $46.37 on a $50,821 base — 0.091%, a bracket-boundary rounding difference between the two engines' rate applications, well inside a per-thousand rounding band. No capital-gains or credit definitional gap remains.

The $46.37 federal liability difference on this tax unit is the exact propagation of the $46.37 tax-before-credits rounding residual above (this case has no offsetting credit or AMT mismatch), so it is the same underlying rounding difference surfaced at the liability total, not an independent liability error.

Single filer, $64,965 wages, negligible ($23.75) short-term capital gain, no other income. Tax-Calculator reports $5,618.61 of tax before credits against PolicyEngine's $5,395.90 — a $222.71 (4.1%) gap with effectively no capital-gains or credit content, so it is not the capital-gains-in-`taxbc` mapping difference the other cases exhibit. The most likely cause is a 2026 ordinary-bracket / standard-deduction parameter-vintage difference between Tax-Calculator 6.7.1 and PolicyEngine-US 1.752.2 (both projecting post-OBBBA 2026 law), but the exact reconciliation is not yet established. Recorded as open.

The $222.71 federal liability difference equals the tax-before-credits difference on this tax unit to the cent (no credit or AMT mismatch), so the liability total carries the same open before-credits residual rather than an independent liability defect.

Married couple with $13,120 wages and $40,081 of self-employment income. Taxable income differs by $129.56 ($14,535.58 vs $14,665.14), which then drives the downstream tax-before-credits and liability gaps. The difference originates in the self-employment adjustments to AGI (the deductible half of SE tax, computed on 92.35% of net earnings), where Tax-Calculator and PolicyEngine apply slightly different SE-tax bases or rounding. The mechanism is identified but the exact $129.56 is not yet reconciled to a documented convention. Recorded as open.

The $51.82 federal liability difference is the exact propagation of the $51.82 tax-before-credits difference, which in turn is the ordinary-rate tax on the $129.56 taxable-income difference above (this is a negative-liability EITC case with no capital-gains, CTC, or AMT mismatch). It is therefore the same self-employment taxable-income difference surfaced downstream, not an independent liability error.

Tax before credits differs by $51.82, which is the ordinary-rate tax on the $129.56 self-employment taxable-income difference recorded above (a marginal rate near 40% at this couple's low taxable income reflects the combined effect of the SE-tax base change). It carries the same open taxable-income root rather than an independent before-credits defect.

Single filer, age 85, with $881,743 long-term capital gain, a $211,306 short-term capital loss, and $17,047 Social Security — roughly $670,000 of net long-term gain. PolicyEngine computes $3,630 of alternative minimum tax; Tax-Calculator computes $0. At this income the AMT exemption is fully phased out, so the divergence is a genuine difference in how the two engines treat net capital gains under the AMT (the preferential-rate stacking and exemption phase-out interaction), not an adapter projection gap — the same capital-gains inputs reach both engines. Recorded as an open triangulation finding for AMT on very-high capital-gains filers.

The $3,630 federal liability difference equals the AMT difference on this tax unit to the cent — every other federal surface (AGI, standard deduction, taxable income, tax before credits, EITC, CTC) matches. The liability gap is therefore entirely the open AMT divergence above surfaced at the total, not an independent liability error.

Married couple, $40,737 earned income, two children under 6, and no capital-gains, self-employment, or AMT content. PolicyEngine reports the full $4,400 Child Tax Credit (2 x $2,200 under 2026 OBBBA law); Tax-Calculator's `ctc_total` reports $4,253.67, a $146.33 shortfall. AGI ($40,737) is far below the $400,000 phase-out and the 15%-of-earnings ACTC refundability limit is not binding (15% x ($40,737 - $2,500) = $5,735 > $4,400), so neither phase-out nor refundability explains the gap. The residual is a Child-Tax-Credit definitional difference between `ctc_total` and PolicyEngine's `ctc_value` that is not yet reconciled. Recorded as open.
